references.text: The parallel text in [ref:Matt 12:31-32|Matthew 12:31-32] is the closest parallel, where Jesus says that all sin and blasphemy will be forgiven people, but blasphemy against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven – neither in this age nor in the coming one.

Mark's version of the same statement in [ref:Mark 3:28-29|Mark 3:28-29] says that all sins will be forgiven the children of men, but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit has no forgiveness forever, but is guilty of an eternal sin.

[ref:Hebr 6:4-6|Hebrews 6:4-6] warns that those who have shared in the Holy Spirit and then fall away cannot be renewed to repentance again – a thematic parallel to the unforgivable sin against the Spirit.

[ref:Hebr 10:26-29|Hebrews 10:26-29] speaks of how whoever sins willfully after receiving knowledge of the truth and has insulted the Spirit of grace shall be judged without mercy. This connects to the seriousness of blaspheming against the Holy Spirit.
[ref:1 Joh 5:16|1 John 5:16] mentions a sin that leads to death, for which one is not urged to pray – something often seen in connection with the unforgivable blasphemy against the Spirit.

The context in [ref:Matt 12:22-24|Matthew 12:22-24] shows that Jesus' words about blasphemy against the Spirit were triggered by the Pharisees attributing the works of the Holy Spirit to Beelzebul – calling God's work the devil's work.

The preceding verse [ref:Luk 12:8-9|Luke 12:8-9] deals with confessing or denying the Son of Man before people, and forms the immediate context for the statement about forgiveness for words against the Son of Man, but not against the Holy Spirit.

[ref:4 Mos 15:30-31|Numbers 15:30-31] speaks of the one who sins with a high hand and insults the Lord – such a person shall be cut off from the people. This is an Old Testament background for deliberate sin that cannot be atoned for.
